title: Ezekiel 43
paragraphs: ¹ Then he led me to the gate — the gate facing east. ² And there was the glory of the God of Israel coming from the east. His voice was like the roar of rushing waters, and the land was radiant with his glory. ³ The vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when he came to destroy the city, and like the vision I had seen by the Chebar River. I fell facedown. ⁴ The glory of the LORD entered the temple through the gate facing east. ⁵ The Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple.

⁶ I heard someone speaking to me from inside the temple, while the man was standing beside me. ⁷ He said to me, "Son of man, this is the place of my throne and the place for the soles of my feet. This is where I will dwell among the Israelites forever. The house of Israel will never again defile my holy name — neither they nor their kings — by their prostitution and by the corpses of their kings at their high places. ⁸ When they placed their threshold next to my threshold and their doorpost beside my doorpost, with only a wall between us, they defiled my holy name by their detestable practices. So I destroyed them in my anger. ⁹ Now let them put away their prostitution and the corpses of their kings far from me, and I will dwell among them forever. ¹⁰ You, son of man, describe the temple to the house of Israel, so they may be ashamed of their sins. Let them study its design.

¹¹ If they are ashamed of all they have done, make known to them the design of the temple — its arrangement, its exits and entrances, its entire design, and all its regulations and instructions. Write it down in their presence so they may faithfully follow its entire design and all its decrees. ¹² This is the law of the temple: all the surrounding area on top of the mountain is most holy. This is the law of the temple. ¹³ These are the measurements of the altar in cubits — the cubit being a standard cubit plus a handwidth: the base is one cubit high and one cubit wide, with a rim of one span around the edge. This is the base of the altar. ¹⁴ From the base at ground level up to the lower ledge is two cubits high and one cubit wide. From the smaller ledge up to the larger ledge is four cubits high and one cubit wide. ¹⁵ The altar hearth is four cubits high, with four horns projecting upward from the hearth.

¹⁶ The altar hearth is twelve cubits long and twelve cubits wide — a perfect square. ¹⁷ The upper ledge is fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits wide, also square, with a rim of half a cubit and a surrounding channel of one cubit. The steps face east." ¹⁸ Then he said to me, "Son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says: These are the regulations for the altar when it is built, for sacrificing burnt offerings and splashing blood on it. ¹⁹ You are to give to the Levitical priests of the family of Zadok, who come near to minister before me, declares the Lord GOD, a young bull as a sin offering. ²⁰ You shall take some of its blood and put it on the four horns of the altar, the four corners of the upper ledge, and the surrounding rim. In this way you will cleanse it and make atonement for it.

²¹ Take the bull for the sin offering and burn it in the designated part of the temple grounds, outside the sanctuary. ²² On the second day offer a male goat without defect as a sin offering. Cleanse the altar as you cleansed it with the bull. ²³ When you have finished the purification, offer a young bull without defect and a ram from the flock without defect. ²⁴ Present them before the LORD, and the priests shall sprinkle salt on them and offer them up as a burnt offering to the LORD. ²⁵ For seven days you shall prepare a goat for a sin offering each day, as well as a young bull and a ram from the flock — all without defect.

²⁶ For seven days they shall purify the altar and consecrate it, and so dedicate it. ²⁷ When these days are over, then from the eighth day onward the priests shall offer on the altar your burnt offerings and your fellowship offerings. I will accept you, declares the Lord GOD.
